stem.en: A message reads AUG GCU UAC GGA UAA. One letter is deleted from the second codon: AUG CUU ACG GAU AA. Kabir says "only the second bead changes". What does the ribosome make?

text.en: Methionine, then leucine, threonine, aspartate, and then it runs off the end without a stop. Every bead after the deletion is different, because the frame shifted.
Methionine, then a different second bead, then tyrosine, glycine, stop.

feedback.en: The ribosome does not know a letter is missing. It reads the next three, and the next, and all of them have moved.

text.en: Nothing; the ribosome detects the missing letter and stops.

feedback.en: It cannot notice. There is no marker for "a letter was here". It reads what it finds.

text.en: Methionine, alanine, tyrosine, glycine, stop, unchanged.

feedback.en: Read the shifted codons yourself. CUU, ACG, GAU. All different.

explanation.en: After a deletion, regroup the letters in threes from the start. Every codon after the change is new. That is a frameshift.
